comments.body:
Just one note that, OBJ importers reading as float would still yields degenerate faces after this fix.
I'm not familiar with the OBJ import landscape though, but since you're preparing this fix, could you comment on how this plays out in your real-world use-case?

Thanks for pointing that out. The translated thin cube in this PR is a synthetic regression case, and I don’t have a production OBJ workflow or third-party importer result to report. In that example, the old exporter writes both X coordinates as `123456`, while the patch writes `123456` and `123456.125`, which are distinct even in float32 (the spacing there is `0.0078125`). With the same thickness at X = `10000000`, the spacing is `1.0`, so a float32 importer can still collapse the two coordinates even when the file preserves them. OpenSCAD’s own OBJ importer parses coordinates as doubles, and the benefit for float32 readers is limited to differences they can represent.

AI assistance was used to prepare this response.

Note that the [OFF specification](http://www.geomview.org/docs/html/OFF.html) does not describe the precision of the ASCII numbers it uses.  (It does mention a binary form that uses 32-bit floats, but I believe we do not support that binary form.)

I'd say that we should write whatever precision we've got, and if the consumer is for some inexplicable reason confused by there being more precision than its internal representation can handle, well, that's the consumer's problem.  Also note that if the consumer gets into trouble because two points are indistinguishable when truncated to 32-bit float, that consumer was never going to handle that model.
